Y12, Y19 good unasked work: INTEG up, STAND down, no reward. Y22 chose daughter over clearance, appraisal dropped. Y25 HR friend explained the CEP, a hidden ceiling decided without me. Y28 put my nine people first, got worst box. Y31 grassroots adviser hinted at politics. Y32 nominated quiet officer, she repaid it Y33. Y34 taught young high-flyer plainly; he will outrank me later. Y35 Perm Sec, asked for team recognition. Y38 added fourth pillar (cost of living) to Engagement report, STAND dropped. Y40 leak on Telegram, cooperated fully with inquiry, appraisal outstanding. Y41 announced quietly built pilot at COS, made it true after; STAND rose. Y42 invited to tea, clearly the politics approach; chose to go. Pattern: promotions keep coming while STAND swings. No rung above Perm Sec, next is 'a different life'. Open questions: does honesty get rewarded, will high-flyer return, what the tea leads to.

best_moment.what: Nominated the quiet officer and she paid it back the next year. It was the one time a kind choice actually came back and felt earned.

worst_moment.what: Put my nine people first and got the worst appraisal box, with no explanation. It felt like the game punishing me for no reason.

skip_year.why: The HR friend explaining the CEP was a lot of acronym talk. It went over my head, and the 'hidden ceiling' reveal only really made sense on the ending card.

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: She repaid the favour in Y33

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y34 taught the young high-flyer plainly
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: He was meant to outrank me later, but I never saw him return, and the legacy line only vaguely nods at people I trained

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y52 took the pen and wrote the statement (my notes only reach Y42, so I only learned of this on the card)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card says it raised my ceiling to Deputy Secretary, which I had no idea about

answer.held_back_by: Probably the hidden ceiling set in my file on day one. I kept doing the right thing and got mixed results, so it felt like the file mattered more than my choices.
answer.ending_fair_why: Perm Sec with a clean record and people who quote me is a decent ending. The reveal that my ceiling was set from the start, and that one choice quietly changed it, was interesting but felt a bit sneaky.
answer.chase_next: The politics route. I went to tea and it seemingly led nowhere, so I want to see what that invitation actually becomes if I say yes to it properly.
answer.play_again_why: 42 years is long, and a lot of it was me tapping through. I'd come back another day, not right now.

tone_breaks.line: No street is named after you and none ever will be, which is rather the point.
tone_breaks.note: Reads like the game nudging me about how clever it is. It's a bit smug but fine.

tone_breaks.line: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
tone_breaks.note: Same kind of smug line, funny but a bit try-hard.

tone_breaks.line: At 52, in The Thing That Actually Happens... raised your ceiling to Deputy Secretary.
tone_breaks.note: My notes say I became Perm Sec at Y35, so a ceiling of Deputy Secretary at 52 doesn't add up. I'm not sure how Perm Sec fits with that.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was about slowly being confirmed and proven in a role, not about big pay. I never really cared about the salary figure.
